A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G. Relocated material can be matched reliably; no material gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic MNL-bandit experiments measuring cumulative regret and runtime in Section 5 and Appendix G, including Figures 1, G.1, and G.2.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments in Section 5 and Appendix G, with the runtime results now displayed as Figure 2.

M1.justification: OFU-MNL++, its adaptive warm-up and restricted-space updates, and the MLE-based OFU-M2NL procedure remain unchanged. Algorithms 1, 2, and F.1 retain the same steps.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic contextual MNL assortment-selection scenarios. The new discussion of reinforcement learning adds related-work context, not evaluated tasks or datasets.

E2.justification: The empirical comparators remain UCB-MNL and TS-MNL (Oh and Iyengar, 2019) and OFU-MNL+ (Lee and Oh, 2024). The comparator membership in the regret and runtime plots is unchanged.

E3.justification: Both retain T=3000, N=50, K=5, B values 2–5, and dimensions d=2 and d=10. Data generation, reward sampling, cumulative-regret measurement, and per-round runtime evaluation are unchanged.

E4.justification: The comparisons across B and the supplementary d=10 results are retained without alteration. Moving the runtime plot from Appendix G to Section 5 introduces no new ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis.

E5.justification: Section 5 retains the statement of 20 independent instances and mean curves with two-standard-deviation shading. Appendix G's independent-run description is also unchanged; no new statistical procedures or seed information appear.

E6.justification: The regret plots in Figures 1 and G.1 are unchanged. v1 Figure G.2 and v4 Figure 2 contain the same runtime curves and uncertainty bands. No result values, rankings, or experimental entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: The assumptions, confidence bounds, regret theorems, and mathematical definitions are unchanged. The text and equations of Appendices B–F match after whitespace normalization; the notation material in Appendix A is retained.

C1.justification: Both retain the same claims about improved online confidence bounds, asymptotically B,K-free variance-dependent regret for OFU-MNL++, and anytime poly(B),K-free regret for OFU-M2NL. Abstract and conclusion wording changes do not alter their scope.

C2.justification: Remark 4.8 newly states that Faury et al. (2022) requires prior knowledge of κ and identifies this as practically difficult. The interpretations of warm-up sensitivity, asymptotic performance, and OFU-M2NL's computational cost were already present, including in Appendix G.

D1.justification: Implementation and parameter descriptions remain unchanged, including Appendix G's data-generation procedure and empirical tuning of the warm-up threshold. No additional tuning ranges, hardware specifications, or code-access information are supplied.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a focused discussion of preference-feedback RL and MNL transition models, with six new references. Remark 4.8 extends the comparison with Faury et al. (2022). These additions broaden context without redefining the central bandit contribution.

P1.justification: v4 corrects the abstract's MLE sentence, rewrites Remark 4.8, adds short related-work and runtime passages, and removes the appendix table of contents. The overall section organization and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The existing runtime plot moves from Figure G.2 in the appendix to Figure 2 beside Figure 1 in the main text, with a revised caption. Table A.1 shifts relative to the notation equations. The plots and table contents remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 makes the existing computational tradeoff easier to assess by bringing the runtime plot and discussion into Section 5, and supplies previously absent context on related RL formulations. These are modest communication improvements; the scientific evidence and reproducibility information are unchanged. Removing the appendix contents slightly weakens navigation, limiting the net gain.
